QF.id: XVI Code of Conduct and Investor Protection_4

question.text: KYC (Know Your Client) requirements for commodity derivatives account opening include:

answer.text: Identity proof, address proof, in-person verification (IPV), PAN/UCC/KRA documentation, and risk categorisation with enhanced due diligence where applicable
Only collecting the client's name and mobile number
KYC is optional for commodity derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series XVI page 193 and pages 195-198 describe KYC for commodity derivatives as requiring identity proof, address proof, in-person verification (IPV), and PAN/UCC/KRA-based documentation, together with client risk categorisation and enhanced due diligence for higher-risk profiles before an account can be opened. The Trap: Name and mobile alone are insufficient. KYC is mandatory, not optional, for commodity derivatives. PAN by itself does not constitute full KYC because the IPV, address proof and KRA steps are also required. Note: Investment objectives are treated by the source as a suitability input for investment advice rather than as a standalone account-opening KYC attribute, so this question stays with the KYC documentation/risk-categorisation set actually listed on pages 193 and 195-198.
